gradients.name: rail
gradients.purpose: The only gradient: navigation rail, mobile drawer, auth brand column.

display.purpose: Signed-out home hero (2.375rem, 3rem at sm, 3.25rem at lg); 404/error pages use 2.25rem, 2.75rem at sm.

headline.purpose: Page title row and auth title (1.75rem, 2rem from lg).

title.purpose: Section headings (1.125rem): SectionHeader, standalone form panels, the home panels and the path page's room list; 1rem for headings in the other ruled panel header rows.

figure.purpose: Figure cells and fixed numbers with tabular lining numerals.

reading.purpose: Room material (.prose-cyber), identical in editor and student view.

label.purpose: Uppercase data field names, columns, figure labels, rail group names; never eyebrows.

button.purpose: All buttons, in Red Hat Display.

mono.purpose: Slugs, IPs, submitted answers, error references at the row's size and weight (usually 400, 0.75 to 0.875rem), no added tracking; code 0.86em inline, 0.84rem in blocks.

serial.purpose: Member serial only: 500, 0.75rem, 0.06em, uppercase, cyan ink.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Only true floating layers: mobile drawer, editor popovers and the collapsed rail's name tooltips.

motion.name: theme
motion.purpose: Background and text colour cross-fade on theme switch; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: rail
motion.purpose: Rail collapse/expand (width, content padding, chevron turn), only when the edge toggle is pressed; a page change renders the saved state with no transition. The collapsed rail's tooltip fades in over 110ms.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: Drawer slide (300ms), page-enter (320ms, 6px rise), check-draw (460ms, 120ms delay).

motion.name: route-progress
motion.purpose: Loading line creeps to 85%, completes in 200ms on arrival.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion all movement and the theme colour cross-fade stop (rail, drawer, nav, page-enter, check-draw, route-progress, progress-fill, theme-switch knob, body cross-fade). Only the 150ms colour transitions on controls, links and fields, the 1px button press, and the editor's 150ms resize-handle fade and swatch-ring change remain.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Rail replaces mobile top bar and drawer.

narrative.overview:
A dark learning console in the Anon Cyber Team logo's colours. Every panel sits flush on one blue-black ground and is separated from its neighbours by a hairline seam, not by a shadow or a gap of empty floating cards. The logo's cyan is a signal rather than a fill: it marks the primary action, the current or next item, links, progress, and focus, so the next room is always one cyan action away. Four status colours each carry one meaning (violet completed, green correct and scores, red retry/error/destructive, amber scheduled), and everything else is calm neutral ink.

The world is the category standard for cybersecurity learning platforms, executed at Hack The Box's level of craft (its seamless flush panels) without copying it and without its green. It is built for long evening reading and answering sessions on laptops and phones: density is moderate, contrast is comfortable, and motion only explains a change of state. Dark is the default; a light theme mirrors the same tokens on a cool white ground. One soft gradient exists, and it lives only on the navigation rail, the mobile drawer, and the auth brand column.

It refuses the hacker costume (neon, glow, terminal green, matrix rain) and the floating rounded-card SaaS dashboard. The previous "Security Paper" world (iris gradient, dot grid, circuit traces, segmented progress ring, rounded floating cards, Archivo) is retired; nothing from it may return.
keyCharacteristics: One blue-black ground, flush panels, 1px hairline seams, no panel shadows.
Logo cyan reserved for forward motion: primary action, current/next/active item, links, progress, focus.
Four single-meaning status colours; a separate identity palette for room/path initials.
One Red Hat family in three cuts: Display for headings, labels, figures and buttons; Text for reading; Mono for machine strings.
Tight corners (6 to 10px); circles only for marks, stop markers, progress tracks, radios, the heatmap's empty-day dot, the lab's empty-target icon ring, the theme switch and scrollbar thumbs.
Dark by default, light by choice, both from the same tokens.

rules.name: The Forward Cyan Rule
rules.body: Logo cyan marks only what moves the member forward or where they are: the primary action, the current/next/active item, links, progress, and focus. One identity accent joins them by owner direction (logo colour on type): the member's first name in the dashboard greeting. It is a signal on type, borders and small fills, never a large decorative fill, never a glow.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Violet means completed, green means correct or a score, red means retry/error/destructive, amber means scheduled. No colour signals anything else, and no two colours share a meaning. Hints are not a state, so hint boxes stay neutral.

rules.name: The Identity Tile Rule
rules.body: Room, path and member-avatar initials tiles use only the identity palette (indigo, teal, raised neutral), so a tile can never be read as a state; state rides on a mark, tag or pill beside the name.

rules.name: The One Token, Two Themes Rule
rules.body: Light and dark come from re-valuing tokens on `:root`, never from hard-coded colours or per-component dark variants (the code block and instructor re-inking are the named exceptions).

rules.name: The Three Cuts Rule
rules.body: Display labels, counts and acts (headings, labels, figures, buttons, titles in rows); Text reads; Mono is only for machine strings and code, never for headings or decoration.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Uppercase labels name data. They never sit above a heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Flush Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels never cast shadows, never float with gutters of empty ground around them as decoration, and never glow. If something must look elevated, it must actually float above other content.

dos: **Do** put panels flush on the ground with 1px seams and 10px corners; separate content with ruled rows, not nested floating cards.
**Do** keep logo cyan for the primary action, the current/next/active item, links, progress and focus (The Forward Cyan Rule).
**Do** give every status exactly one colour: violet completed, green correct/score, red retry/error/destructive, amber scheduled.
**Do** use identity tiles (indigo, teal, neutral) for room and path initials.
**Do** set headings, labels, figures and buttons in Red Hat Display, reading in Red Hat Text, and serials, slugs, error references and code in Red Hat Mono.
**Do** build both themes from the same tokens; test every new surface in dark and light.
**Do** keep 44px targets and 16px field text on coarse pointers and a visible 2px cyan-ink focus outline.

**Do** limit motion to state changes: 150 to 320ms for transitions, with `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for arrivals. The only longer ones are the progress-bar fill (500ms), the one-time check draw (460ms after a 120ms delay) and the route loading line's slow creep; the only shorter one is the rail tooltip's 110ms fade-in. Honour reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** add a second gradient; the rail gradient lives only on the rail, mobile drawer and auth brand column.
**Don't** put shadows on panels; lift belongs only to the drawer, editor popovers and the collapsed rail's tooltips.
**Don't** use neon, glow, terminal green, matrix effects or a hacker costume.
**Don't** bring back anything from the retired Security Paper world: iris gradient, dot grid, circuit traces, segmented progress ring, rounded floating cards, Archivo.
**Don't** fill large areas with cyan or use a status colour for anything but its one meaning.
**Don't** place uppercase labels above headings as eyebrows or kickers.
**Don't** use emoji or glyph characters as icons; draw stroked inline SVG beside a label.
**Don't** put arrows on buttons that do not move the member forward or back.
